scenes.caption: What if burying your brother meant choosing death? A tragedy by Sophocles, the Athenian playwright, follows Antigone, a sister who defies the king, after a civil war. One brother is praised as a defender of the city; the other is branded a traitor. Creon, the ruler who forbids burial, leaves the traitor's body exposed outside Thebes.
scenes.emotional_turn: The scene moves from battlefield after fighting to Antigone staring across dust, creating shock and indignation.

motivation.goal: Antigone wants her brother buried with dignity
motivation.obstacle: Creon brands him a traitor and forbids the rites
motivation.stakes: her family loses its final duty and she risks death by resisting

scenes.caption: Ismene warns her that defying the decree means death. But Antigone believes a brother does not stop being family because a king calls him an enemy. Without burial rites, the dead are denied the rest their family owes them, so she goes alone, carrying dust to bury him in secret.
scenes.emotional_turn: The scene moves from sisters arguing in shadow to palm releasing earth over body, creating fear becoming resolve.

motivation.goal: Antigone wants to perform the burial herself
motivation.obstacle: Ismene fears the king's punishment and refuses to join her
motivation.stakes: Antigone must choose between safety and loyalty to her dead brother

scenes.caption: The guards catch her scattering dust over the body. Before Creon, she admits what she has done. He believes sparing a traitor would weaken his rule; she believes obeying him would betray her family. Neither will yield.
scenes.emotional_turn: The scene moves from guard seizing Antigone to Creon pointing toward prison, creating defiance against power.

motivation.goal: Antigone wants to defend the burial as a family duty
motivation.obstacle: Creon treats her act as rebellion against his new rule
motivation.stakes: neither can retreat without surrendering the principle that guides them

scenes.caption: Creon orders her sealed alive inside a rocky tomb. His son Haemon pleads for mercy, warning that the city will turn against a king who punishes devotion. Creon hears only disobedience, and the last chance to reverse the sentence slips away.
scenes.emotional_turn: The scene moves from Haemon reaching toward father to stone opening sealed, creating hopelessness.

motivation.goal: Haemon wants Creon to spare Antigone
motivation.obstacle: Creon mistakes his warning for disobedience
motivation.stakes: the tomb will become a sentence no apology can undo

scenes.caption: Only when Tiresias warns that the gods reject Creon's decree does he relent. He hurries toward the tomb, but Antigone is already dead. Haemon dies beside her, and grief follows him back into the palace.

motivation.obstacle: Tiresias's warning comes after Antigone has already died
motivation.stakes: his delay destroys Haemon as well as the woman he condemned

scenes.caption: Creon survives with the power he defended and the family his decree destroyed. Antigone could not defeat the king, but his victory leaves him alone with the cost of being obeyed.
scenes.emotional_turn: The scene moves from vacant royal chair to dawn over silent Thebes, creating moral devastation.

motivation.goal: Creon wants to preserve the authority he defended
motivation.obstacle: his decree has destroyed his own family and emptied his victory
motivation.stakes: he must live with the human cost of being obeyed
